dataset.name: Hamrah Community Signal Candidates - Australia Study
dataset.note: These are candidate community signals extracted from the uploaded source. They are not official eligibility rules or validated Hamrah Store signals.

signals.signal: Student visa processing for Iranian applicants appears highly variable and difficult to predict.

evidence.summary: An applicant reported approximately 100 days since lodgement with no update.

counter_evidence.summary: Another community member reported that their visa had recently been granted.
A community member stated that multiple applicants had received grants in under one month.

signals.interpretation: The available evidence supports high variance and uncertainty rather than a general visa freeze or universal long delay.

signals.signal: Monash EOI screening may apply strict academic filters and can produce very rapid rejections.

evidence.summary: An applicant with GPA 17.5/20 reported rejection within about 10 minutes and said follow-up indicated GPA was the reason.
Another applicant reported an EOI rejection approximately 20 minutes after submission.

signals.interpretation: The reports are consistent with a fast pre-screen process, but they do not establish a universal GPA threshold across all Monash faculties or supervisors.

signals.signal: Visa feasibility may, in some cases, affect university admission decisions before the visa stage.

evidence.summary: A master's applicant reported that RMIT told them the rejection was not due to GPA or CV but because they were unlikely to obtain a visa.

signals.interpretation: This is a single self-report and should not be treated as a general RMIT admissions policy.

signals.signal: Direct PhD entry from an Iranian bachelor's degree may face structural difficulty where an Honours-equivalent qualification is expected.

evidence.summary: A channel adviser stated that direct PhD exists but commonly requires a bachelor's Honours qualification and described this as difficult for applicants educated in Iran.

signals.interpretation: This is a community/adviser statement and not a verified rule applying identically to every Australian university or PhD program.

signals.signal: Full funding for master's study appears high-friction and strongly dependent on research profile and research-master eligibility.

evidence.summary: A channel adviser stated that full funding at master's level is very difficult and requires a strong profile, with funding concentrated in research-oriented master's routes.
The same adviser suggested applicants with strong research experience try research master's programs, otherwise self-funded master's study may be the practical alternative.

signals.interpretation: The source supports 'difficult and profile-sensitive', not 'impossible'.

signals.signal: Incomplete documentation may create significant friction because university admissions teams may provide limited flexibility when stated requirements are not met.

evidence.summary: A channel adviser stated that Australian university admissions offices are not very accommodating when required documents are incomplete.

signals.interpretation: This is operational community guidance rather than an official universal admissions rule.
